turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with compound_id, CLint_uL_per_min_mg, and molecular_weight columns for your 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs (e.g., imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, ponatinib)
Key steps:

PKNCA scaling engine → converts CLint_microsomal to intrinsic clearance using microsomal protein binding and MPPGL scaling factors
Well-stirred model + parallel-tube model → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg) per compound
Extraction ratio calculator → E = CLh / Qh (hepatic blood flow ~20.7 mL/min/kg) per compound


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + extraction ratio per compound, both models) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison + high/intermediate/low extraction classification)

Decision gate: Extraction ratio E > 0.7 = high-extraction compound (flow-limited, CLh ≈ Qh); E < 0.3 = low-extraction (enzyme-limited, sensitive to protein binding changes and enzyme inhibition/induction). Flag any TKI with E > 0.7 for hepatic blood flow sensitivity in PK modeling.

turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance (Well-Stirred Model) — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance and extraction ratio for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs — Dasatinib (CLint=220 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Bosutinib (CLint=60 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.03), Imatinib (CLint=25 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Nilotinib (CLint=12 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.01); model parameters: Qh=20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic=1.0
Key steps:

PKNCA scaling engine → converts CLint_microsomal (μL/min/mg) to CLint_scaled (mL/min/kg) using MPPGL (45 mg/g liver) and liver weight (25.7 g/kg body weight)
Well-stirred model → CLh = (Qh × fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) per compound → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg)
Extraction ratio calculator → E = CLh / Qh per compound → high/intermediate/low classification


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + extraction ratio per compound) + clearance_summary.json (extraction class per TKI + model parameters used)

Decision gate: E > 0.7 = high-extraction (flow-limited; Dasatinib most likely to exceed this threshold given CLint=220); E < 0.3 = low-extraction (enzyme-limited; Nilotinib most likely candidate — sensitive to CYP3A4 inhibition and plasma protein binding shifts). Flag high-extraction TKIs for first-pass effect and hepatic blood flow variability in downstream PK modeling.

ABL1 Pharmacophore Build & Library Screen — Derives a consensus pharmacophore from four ABL1 inhibitors and scores a compound library against it in a single workflow.


Input: Reference SMILES — Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib; Library SMILES — Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen; min_features = 3


Key steps:

Pharmacophore → builds consensus feature model (H-bond donors/acceptors, hydrophobic centers, aromatic rings, charged groups) from the 4 reference ABL1 inhibitors
Pharmacophore Alignment → aligns each library compound to the model, computes per-feature match scores and overall pharmacophore fit score



Expected output: Ranked hit list (CSV) with per-compound feature-match scores, a pharmacophore model file (.phar or .json), and a visual alignment report — compounds matching ≥ 3 features flagged as hits


Decision gate: Retain compounds with ≥ 3 matched pharmacophoric features AND a fit score above the consensus threshold; expect Gleevec-analog-1 and Ponatinib to pass (structurally similar to reference inhibitors), while Terfenadine and Acetaminophen are predicted to fail as negative controls.
